how: The starter proposes a mark and supplies an anchor that another member commits to placing.
Calls recruit additional hands for defence and erasure through existing class Facebook groups.
A request for mutual help receives a bare commitment to join.
Moderators consolidate canvas posts and redirect later requests to a sticky.
Participants propose the M and Ski-U-Mah, widen the logo, and alter letter widths to fit.
Builders seed the mark and report completion of the M, border, and widening.
Coordinates and official templates guide placements while participants urge builders to follow one plan.
Participants request bot code and report shared bots maintaining several logos.
Members repair stray changes, prefer upkeep to growth, interrupt redesign under attack, and recall overnight guarding.
Neighbours propose non-vandalism, exchanged protection, relocation assistance, and room-sharing bargains.
Participants prohibit attacks on college neighbours and apologise for taking another group's area.
Members ask for help, join neighbours, promise reciprocity, thank helpers, and sometimes refuse assistance.
Participants call for a shared college corner and joint logo while debating the breadth of their alliance.
Participants call for converting rival lettering, erasing another school, and finishing a rival off.
Participants claim joint victory and later recount wins over named opponents.
A participant judges an enlargement too risky because too few people are online.
Abandoning a proposed additional inscription and reporting a neighbour's move do not establish relocation of the room's own lost home.
Completion prompts celebration, congratulations, and retrospective claims of individual guarding labour.
Members propose a development history, announce the end, and recount the fate of their work.
Recounting completed work does not establish a decision to continue the collective or move it to a later canvas.
Members recognise a new-logo April Fools prank, report being fooled, and preserve its reveal.
A pseudo-general's self-description and posting moderation cannot establish canvas command or test a cross-room prevalence claim.
Attack calls name school rivals and explicitly use league membership to mark who should be excluded.
Alliance disagreement does not state that an envoy lacks authority to bind other placers.
A misplaced-pixel observation does not establish a cleanup request or a dispute over which preserved version should survive.
Rival names and hostility during the canvas do not document an earlier quarrel's origin.
Members invoke their shared college affiliation and distinguish Minnesota from Michigan.
A builder interprets erased work as a neighbouring flag threatening the M.
Offering another group rebuilding room does not establish an ongoing guest arrangement under a host's rules.
A member reports carrying a relocation-and-help offer to another room in Spanish.
The initial M proposal provides an existing project for a later call to build the inscription.
A supplied anchor is followed by an explicit commitment to place the seed pixel.
The visible request-and-acceptance pair supports a bare joining response without proving silent assent or the proposed preference mechanism.
Consolidation and redirection are explicit, but the concepts do not identify a recruitment-caused flood as their motive.
A posted design settles collective practice only insofar as builders receive and follow its current version.
Reported completion is followed by commitments to maintain the design and repair stray changes.
Perceived opposing automation explicitly prompts a request for code without establishing measured exhaustion of manual upkeep capacity.
A perceived flag threat to the M is followed by an explicit relocation-and-help offer, without proof that negotiation caused retreat.
Cooperation is invoked to discourage attacks, but the concepts do not identify settled border terms causing compliance.
A maintenance-related request yields assistance only when participants accept the exchange, which can depend on a protection guarantee.
Movement and an offered trade must remain distinguishable from accepted aid because a neighbour's withdrawal can coexist with a refusal to help.
A call to save the shared logo is followed by an explicit appeal for conference unity against the threat.
Recruitment can explicitly seek erasure in the initial call rather than require a later switch from building to attacking.
A renewed attack call receives a bare challenge that questions whether the rival should be allowed space.
A treaty packages attack with mutual restoration, but the concepts do not establish an attack call causing a subsequent deal.
Attack calls are followed by claims of joint victory over the same opponent.
Completion reporting and celebration can occur within the same turn rather than form separate sequential stages.
A proposed history and completion congratulations show recording beside celebration but do not establish the proposed causal transition.
The documented history proposal and retrospective account do not show an ensuing decision to sustain the temporary collective.
Scarcity affecting optional enlargement must be distinguished from scarcity affecting an overrun home before predicting relocation.
A truce proposal and disagreement over coalition membership do not document a challenge to who may bind the room.
Updating the public plan can follow haphazard construction, requiring repeated repair of shared instructions rather than one final template.
Redesign requiring a shared understanding can be set aside in favour of defending the existing form when participants cannot coordinate the change.
A treaty can combine removing a third party with reciprocal restoration instead of making negotiation an alternative to attack.
A proposed shared affiliation becomes a coalition only to the extent participants accept it despite narrower loyalties and internal fighting.
A proposed coordination chat must be distinguished from actual automation and does not establish either chat migration or script execution.
